content: This long-term technology possesses the potential to significantly enhance operational efficiency and reduce congestion at logistical toll collection points, marking a critical step in the development of intelligent tolling systems that support industrial operations . Insights from the April 2026 International Bridge, Tunnel and Turnpike Association Technology Summit further underscore an industry-wide push toward implementation-focused discussions on these evolving systems, emphasizing a practical approach to leveraging next-generation technologies for comprehensive toll management [15] . This massive expansion is fundamentally tied to the widespread global adoption of electronic tolling technologies, which are systematically replacing traditional, manual systems and reflecting the steady uptake of automated methods across industrial and logistical networks [13][14] . Although some historical sources, such as older administrative toll adjustment processes, offer limited details on recent technology evolution and instead focus on procedural adjustments, the overarching trajectory of the industry is clear [11] . The adoption of technology in both mineral toll processing and logistical toll management increasingly aligns with broader industry goals of maximal efficiency, data transparency, and sustainability, as extensively discussed in recent industry summits . This dual focus on metallurgical innovation and supply chain automation ensures that toll processing operations can maximize yield while minimizing overhead and environmental impact. The ongoing pace and scope of these technological implementations remain subject to continuous refinement, with strong forecasts of sustained innovation and market growth shaping the regional industry well beyond 2026 [12][13][14][15] . Ultimately, the successful integration of these diverse processing and operational technologies dictates the competitive viability of toll processing facilities operating within South Africa's dynamic industrial sector.
